_derived: An excerpt, not the whole answer. The source is the Debian security tracker's dump, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/data/json, downloaded on 2026-10-09 at 12:47 UTC (82,378,232 bytes, 4067 source packages). Kept: three source packages — nginx, openssh and openssh-gssapi — and within each one CVE: nginx CVE-2026-90439, which the tracker marks resolved in trixie and bookworm with fixed_version "0", its spelling for a version that was never affected; openssh CVE-2026-106585, open in trixie with a no-dsa note; and openssh-gssapi CVE-2026-106585, which the tracker lists for sid and forky only, since the package is not in trixie. Every kept entry is copied verbatim; nothing was added or changed, only left out.

CVE-2026-90439.description: NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source have a vulnerability in the ngx_http_v3_module module. When using HTTP/3 with OpenSSL versions <= OpenSSL 3.5.0 under certain configurations, a limited heap buffer overflow could happen while processing a TLS handshake. This can happen in a non-deterministic manner that is beyond the attacker's control. This may cause a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process leading to a restart and/or limited data corruption.  Impact: This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or limited data corruption. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.     Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

CVE-2026-106585.description: In sshd and ssh in OpenSSH before 10.6, there is no check for whether the maximum packet length is exceeded during decompression of highly compressed data.
